name: Nethanel
overview: Nethanel was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the fifth-born son of Obed-edom. His mention in Scripture is concise, highlighting his place within a Levitical family without additional narrative detail or specific roles.
namesAndTitles: The name Nethanel means 'G-d [El] has given,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning common among Hebrew names. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:4, underscores the recognition of divine provision or blessing, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Nethanel is explicitly recorded as the son of Obed-edom. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Nethanel's significance lies in his identification as a descendant of Obed-edom within the tribe of Levi, a tribe set apart for service to the Lord. His mention in 1 Chronicles situates him within the genealogical framework that supports the organization and duties of the Levitical families, underscoring the continuity of God’s appointed servants in Israel.
